reading.body:
Perplexity Enterprise Pro trades consumer speed for data controls: same retrieval-augmented engine, but with SSO, admin dashboards, and explicit training opt-out, priced per seat annually.

The product solves a specific problem for regulated organizations. You get the citing-answer model that works in the consumer tier, but wrapped in the governance layer that compliance teams require: data retention controls, audit visibility into seat usage, and a contractual promise that your inputs do not feed model retraining. The admin dashboard gives you inventory—which matters when you are trying to count AI tools actually in use rather than pilots no one touches.

The pricing model creates a friction point that does not exist in the free tier. Per-seat annual contracts make sense for budgeting, but they require you to predict adoption before you know it. If you undersize, you pay more per head. If you oversize, you have unused seats and governance questions about why. This is standard enterprise software behavior, not specific to Perplexity.

Citations remain the core claim and the core limitation. The product retrieves sources and shows them to you. That is useful for audit trails and for blocking obvious hallucinations. It does not make the sources reliable; your team still reads them. The enterprise tier does not change that burden.

governance_note: Same evidentiary point as the consumer product, now under admin control. The admin dashboard tells you which seats are active and what the usage looks like, which matters for the AI inventory. Citations are still leads, not evidence, and that rule does not change with the tier.
training_optout: Enterprise Pro explicitly excludes customer data from model training. Verify the current contract terms.
